title: Delegated guardband and permission canvas for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a second-generation RBAC model that supports delegated admin boundaries (guardbands), a compact permission canvas for UI/CLI, SSO/SAML attribute-to-role mappings, and audit anchoring requirements. This ticket produces a spec and a migration path for existing role/permission data, plus an API contract for enforcement and for the Console UI to render a permission matrix.
approach: We will model authorization as a three-layer tuple: (actor, resource-path, capability). Resource-paths are hierarchical strings (org/project/environment/asset). Guardbands are lightweight, declarative constraints attached to role bindings that limit elevation scope without creating new roles. The API exposes canonical operations: authorize, list-effective-roles, explain-decision. SAML/SSO will map incoming assertions to 'role-intent' claims which the control-plane resolves into concrete bindings at auth-time.
permission_matrix_preview:
Example rows (resource pattern -> allowed capabilities):
- org/* -> [view, list, billing:read] (Org admins)
- org/*/project/* -> [view, deploy, logs:read] (Project operators)
- org/*/project/*/env/* -> [exec, kv:read, kv:write?guarded] (Env runtime)
Guardband example: binding 'team-deployers' -> role 'project-operator' with guardband 'no-billing=true; max-ttl=1h'
Explanation API example: explain(actor, resource, action) -> [allowed|denied, matched-bindings, reason, audit-snapshot-id]
design_decision_log: Favor small number of canonical capabilities over large combinatorial actions to keep the console matrix manageable.
Guardbands chosen instead of proliferating roles to enable safe delegation across tenants.
Use hierarchical resource string instead of numeric IDs for easier pattern matching and cross-tenant policies.
Audit snapshots (immutable) are recorded for every allow/deny decision that crosses an admin guardband or affects a privileged capability.
audit_requirements: Record decision context including actor id, raw SAML assertion id (when present), resolved effective roles, matched guardbands, input TTL, resource path, and capability.
Persist immutable audit-snapshot-id in write-ahead log for 90 days (configurable per-customer).
Expose SAML mapping events to external SIEM via syslog/Kafka sink for enterprise customers.
saml_mapping_notes: Accept both 'roles' and 'role-intent' attributes. If role-intent is present, run resolution pipeline to map to current role catalog (supports fuzzy name matches and namespace prefixes).
Support attribute-to-binding rules with precedence: explicit binding overrides default role mapping. Store mapping version in audit snapshot.
Fallback behavior: unknown roles in SAML assertion result in a deny with helpful error and a suggest-binding link in the Console.
admin_controls: Breakglass flows: time-limited temporary elevation issuing a traceable temporary-binding with TTL and mandatory justification.
Canary admin role: 'support-admin' with read-only incident playbooks plus ability to open temporary elevation requests via API.
Immutable owner: resource owners can only be changed via multi-actor approval (2 approvals) and recorded as an auditable event.
migration_plan: Export current role bindings and permissions from the monolith service and normalize to (principal, resource-path, capability) tuples.
Run offline simulation for 2 weeks: feed production request logs into the new policy engine in 'observe-only' mode and collect explain traces for false positives/negatives.
Iterate on guardband rule templates to cover 90th percentile of exceptions from simulation.
Deploy enforcement behind feature flag + canary to 10% of requests, monitor 401/403 deltas and audit log volume, then ramp.
Cutover: schedule maintenance window for customers with strict SLAs; for others, do gradual migration with automatic rollback on elevated error budgets.
success_criteria: API contract published and accepted by SDK owners
Console renders permission canvas for at least org and project levels
Migration simulation shows <=0.5% actionable denies on non-privileged traffic
Audit snapshots captured for all guardband-crossing decisions in canary rollout
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc + OpenAPI contract merged, sample SAML mapping config present in repo, runbooks for breakglass and owner-change created, end-to-end demo with canary flag toggled and audit traces visible in ELK.
